text:
Nico Hischier passed 500 career points last weekend, with a shorthanded goal in a 7-4 win in Washington, and NHL.com is calling his two-way game elite. It's hard to argue. The 2017 first overall pick has 9 goals and 15 points in 22 games on 18 minutes a night, and New Jersey gets about 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five.

His own finishing is exactly on target: 9 goals on 9.0 expected. The part that's been unlucky is everyone around him. The Devils have scored 4.6 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which is why his assist total (6) looks thin for a top-line center. That usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey saw the same thing last season, with his chance-based value well ahead of his actual results, while he drove play against top competition.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a signature: a fifth of his setups come from behind the net, more than double a typical forward. Watch for it. When those passes start landing in the back of the net, the points will follow.
